scenario.highLevelScenario: Reference data not exists -NACK- LE are incorrect -
scenario.expectedErrorMessage: Reference data / Legal Entity does not exist
notes: BNKA-ABC against BNKB-HK: BNKA-ABC is a legal entity whose reference data does not exist in Baton, which is the point of the row. Everything else is an ordinary CNH / USD spot trade between PVP parties (CRDS relation PVP; pvpIntent and stmIntent true for both sides), so the legal entity is the only thing that is wrong.

The trade runs to step 05b, not 05: the step order is 4, 5, 5b, so stopping at 5 would skip the Domain B check. Steps 05 and 05b are declared to fail, so the NACK is proven on both domains rather than just the injecting one.
Step 04 is declared to pass: the simulator takes the trade and the rejection happens downstream, so the trade never reaches either ledger and test_trade_found_on_ledger fails in 05 and 05b.

Those declared failures are written into the HTML report as passed and do not count against the exit code. If either step PASSES, the runner turns it into a failure instead, because a trade with a legal entity Baton does not know reaching the ledger means the rejection stopped happening.

The ledger lookups in 05 and 05b cannot see the NACK itself, so they prove the rejection by the trade's absence. The sheet gives no error code; its expected result is recorded as expectedErrorMessage.

The sheet states the trade as USD-CNH: base 1234 USD, reference 8317.16 CNH. It is carried as CNHUSD, the order the rest of the pack and TradeServ use, with each amount kept on its own currency: 8317.16 CNH (baseCurrencyAmount) and 1234 USD (referenceCurrencyAmount).

direction and Against list both options in the sheet (Buy/Sell, Base/Reference). The side is taken from the trade TradeServ actually published for this row, in the 25 Sep and 5 Oct exports: BNKA-ABC buys 8317.16 CNH from BNKB-HK and pays 1234 USD. So BNKA-ABC is the base currency (CNH) buyer and partyDirection is Buy, which is Buy against the sheet's Reference currency; direction and against above record that choice. Step 04 checks the buyer, seller and partyDirection agree.

Were the trade to reach the ledgers, Domain A (BNKA-ABC) would show CNH BUY / USD SELL and Domain B (BNKB-HK) the reverse; steps 05 and 05b assert those sides, but are expected to fail before them at the ledger lookup.
It is written as a one-entry trades list rather than a bare trade, because only a trades entry carries runUpTo and expect through to the runner.
Settlement is the current date and tradeDate is the run date, both resolved from the run clock.
tradeReference, tradeReferenceSupplement and counterpartyReferenceNumber are free-text boxes, so they are generated per run as tradeId, the party partyTradeId and the counterparty partyTradeId.
ccpAlias, clearingBroker and counterpartyClearingBroker are blank in the sheet and have no wrapper field, so they are left out of the payload entirely.
Party CCP (STMPVP) and Cpty CCP (STMPVP) are legal-entity reference data in Baton, not trade fields, so they are recorded here and the payload carries the ordinary PVP settlement flag.
settlementCcy (USD) has no field in the wrapper, so it is recorded here only.
rate is carried as the sheet states it (2) even though 8317.16/1234 implies 6.74.
